answer.rationale: Verify whether market benchmarking and a longer-term volume commitment can bring the incumbent close to the 18% savings mandate while preserving delivery continuity. With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, switching primary supply could create disproportionate disruption risk. A guarded negotiation preserves the incumbent’s integration and delivery stability while testing whether cost savings are achievable; if not, the unresolved gap should remain explicit rather than assuming the low-cost quote eliminates total-cost risk.
